PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: loc-fissure-shaft
Workflow profile: 2X3_VERTICAL (2:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Location guard: transfer only color, light behavior, haze, scale language, and material realism. Do not copy the reference cave, Hell gate, fortress geometry, crowds, or blocking unless this row explicitly requires those elements.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
VERTICAL FISSURE / DESCENT SHAFT — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: CINEMATIC ENVIRONMENT, SCALE, LIGHTING, MATERIALS, AND CONTINUITY.

Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Cinematic biblical epic location production reference of the vertical fissure and descent shaft that opens the harrowing of Hell: a purposeful vertical wound in desert earth, approximately forty feet (twelve meters) in diameter at the surface rim, plunging into indeterminate spiritual depth rather than a measurable geological pit. Photoreal live-action set design, not illustration, not concept-art stylization, not CGI cartoon geometry. Aspect framing intended for 2.39:1 widescreen production stills.

Surface geometry: the shaft mouth is an irregular but cleanly torn circular-to-oval rupture through packed desert crust and stone, edges split with purpose rather than random earthquake violence. Rim soil is dry ochre and ash-gray grit, cracked into polygonal plates that tilt slightly inward; fractured bedrock shelves step down a few feet before the true vertical drop begins. No modern debris, no tools, no rails, no ladders, no ropes, no metal hardware of any contemporary kind—only ancient earth and stone. Beyond the rim, a strip of night desert may be barely suggested: bruised purple-black sky, sparse cold starlight, thin dust hanging motionless as if the world is holding its breath.

Wall architecture: the primary cylinder is polished-black obsidian-like stone, glass-hard and faintly translucent at thin edges, with deep conchoidal fractures and vertical striations running down into darkness. Through the black mineral run irregular veins of dying embers—dull red-orange coals and ember-lines embedded in the rock, glowing weakly like residual heat from an ancient furnace, not bright torch fire. Embers cluster in hairline seams, some already cooling to charcoal gray, others still breathing faint red underglow. Occasional crystalline specular highlights catch the descending light on glossy facets. Moisture is minimal; instead the air holds dry ash, fine black dust, and thin smoke that drifts slowly upward against the shaft’s downward visual pull.

Embedded wall faces (continuity-critical environmental detail): ancient faces of trapped souls press out from within the obsidian, partially fused with the stone as if the walls themselves are prison. Faces appear at irregular intervals around the full circumference and down into depth—forehead, cheek, and mouth emerging from mineral, eyes open and turned upward toward the surface light with impossible hope rather than pure agony. Skin tones read as pale ash and stone-dusted flesh, half-mineralized, with dust and fine cracks across brows and lips. Each face has only one face on the front of the head; no rear faces, no duplicate faces on the back of any head, no grotesque multi-face mutations. Expressions are reverent, longing, almost prayerful—watching the descent path as if sensing deliverance. These faces are environmental architecture, not a crowd of free-standing figures in the void.

Depth and spatial reading: looking nearly straight down the axis of the shaft (or from a high three-quarter overhead angle that still reads as a vertical descent environment), the cylinder narrows only slightly with atmospheric perspective, then dissolves into absolute darkness far below. No visible floor, no gate at the bottom in this asset—only infinite depth and the sense of a spiritual corridor between earth and Hell’s fortress. Mid-shaft, faint red underglow from the ember veins and a colder residual blue-black ambient from the abyss below create layered recession. Scale is monumental: a human figure, if imagined, would be tiny against the forty-foot mouth; the walls feel cathedral-tall and endless.

Lighting design (locked continuity for this beat): mixed mid-descent state between cold earth night and divine intrusion. From the open rim above, a first column of divine golden radiance begins to stream downward—not ordinary sunlight, but older ethereal gold and warm amber god rays (#FFD700 / #FFBF00 character), approximately 6500K at core with soft amber falloff, volumetric and particulate-laden. Rays cut clean shafts through suspended ash and smoke, creating visible beams that slide along glossy obsidian facets and skim the upward-turned wall faces. Rim fill remains colder: starlight and night air near 5000K, cool purple-black spill at the lip. Embers provide localized 3000–3500K red points along seams. The lower third of the frame sinks into deep crimson-tinged black (#8B0000 residual in shadow edges) and pure obsidian black (#0A0A0A). Avoid pure flat darkness without form; keep wall geometry readable via speculars and ember veins even where divine light has not yet reached.

Atmosphere and particles: thick atmospheric depth from ash flakes, fine stone dust, and thin smoke columns rising against the light. Particles catch golden rays as bright motes and longer streaks; in shadow they read as gray-black grit. Occasional larger ash fragments drift like black snow. Subtle heat shimmer near stronger ember veins. Air should feel heavy, ancient, and charged—poison-realm residue mixed with the first breath of divine perfume suggested only by light warmth, not by modern effects language.

Camera and lens language: production still looking down into the vertical shaft as a primary hero location plate—approximately 24–35mm wide vertical or high-angle descent framing, deep focus on near rim and mid-wall faces with atmospheric falloff into infinite depth; optional slight dutch-free, sacred, axial composition emphasizing the wound’s purposeful geometry. Physically coherent parallax of wall faces and ember seams. No lens brand names, no anamorphic flare logos, no UI. Mild cinematic contrast, controlled highlight bloom only on divine rays and the brightest ember cores.

Color grade: deep crimsons and obsidian blacks in the lower shaft and wall recesses; cold blue-black ambient in unlit cavities; ethereal golds and warm amber in the descending volumetric column; desaturated desert ochres only at the distant rim. Transition reads as divine light invading a hell-adjacent mineral throat. Photoreal material response: obsidian speculars, matte ash, rough mineralized flesh of wall faces, soft volumetric scattering in dust.

Continuity locks: surface diameter ~40 feet; walls are obsidian veined with dying embers; ancient trapped faces press from stone watching upward with hope; depth feels infinite; divine golden light streams from above creating dramatic contrast with surrounding darkness; no gate, fortress, guardians, or full character hero figures required in this environment plate (empty sacred shaft or at most implied scale); no modern objects, scaffolding, text, captions, logos, watermarks, borders, or readable inscriptions on stone. Sacred biblical-epic tone—reverent, monumental, spiritually charged—not gore-porn, not campy fantasy dungeon, not sci-fi portal. One face only on the front of any head. Photoreal live-action production reference quality suitable for Krea 2 Turbo / Qwen3-VL generation and later matching plates for descent, Jesus arrival light, and fissure seal beats.
